one_liner: Header-only C++20 rank/select bit vector: 8% faster rank, 16.5% faster select than cs-poppy.
what_it_does: Provides an uncompressed bit vector (pasta::BitVector) plus separate rank/select support structures (Rank/RankSelect, FlatRank/FlatRankSelect, WideRank/WideRankSelect for vectors up to 2^40 bits) built on top of it. These answer 'how many set bits before position i' (rank) and 'position of the j-th set bit' (select), operations std::bitset and std::vector<bool> don't offer. Not drop-in: you build the bit vector, then wrap it in a chosen support structure and query through that object.
how_it_is_fast: Uses a two-level (L1/L2) block metadata layout in the lineage of cs-poppy (Zhou, Andersen & Kaminsky, SEA'13), with 512-bit L2 blocks, tuned to hold the same ~3.51% space overhead while improving cache-friendliness of the 'flat' layout. The select path can locate the target L2 block with x86-64 SIMD intrinsics (FindL2FlatWith::INTRINSICS, compiled under __x86_64__) instead of linear or binary search over block summaries, which is where most of the select speedup comes from.
when_to_use: Need succinct rank/select over a static, uncompressed bit vector (e.g., building an FM-index or other compact text index)
Already using or evaluating cs-poppy-style compact rank/select structures and want the same space overhead with somewhat faster queries
Target is x86-64 and can compile with -march=native to get the SIMD-accelerated select path
Single-threaded/sequential query workload (paper's benchmarks are single-core)
C++20 codebase where GPL-3.0 header-only vendoring is acceptable
when_not_to_use: Need a std::bitset/std::vector<bool>-compatible API — this is a separate type with its own construction and query interface, not a drop-in replacement
License must be MIT/BSD-permissive — this is GPL-3.0, more restrictive than the sibling libraries in this category
Rank-only workload where extra memory is acceptable — sdsl-v and rank9select answer rank faster but use 1.75-6.98x more space (per verification notes)
Stuck on C++17 or earlier, or on a non-x86-64 platform where the SIMD select path is unavailable
Need an actively maintained dependency — single-author project, last commit 2025-04-07, only 36 stars

integration.dependencies: tlx (github.com/tlx/tlx) and pasta-toolbox/utils, both pulled automatically via CMake FetchContent when building tests/benchmarks; no git submodules
integration.min_toolchain: C++20; CMake 3.25 to build tests/benchmarks via the provided presets (paper's benchmarks used GCC 10.2)
integration.platforms: x86-64 for the SIMD-accelerated select path (FindL2FlatWith::INTRINSICS, gated on __x86_64__); a non-intrinsic linear/binary-search fallback exists for other architectures but is not the configuration benchmarked in the paper
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: false — cs-poppy itself isn't a stdlib facility, and this library's API (separate BitVector + support-structure wrapper) differs from cs-poppy's; std::bitset/std::vector<bool> have no rank/select at all, so there's no drop-in relationship there either

gotchas: Support structures (e.g. FlatRankSelect) are constructed from an existing BitVector instance and query through that wrapper; build the bit vector first, then attach the rank/select structure you need

Multiple rank/select variants exist (Rank/RankSelect, FlatRank/FlatRankSelect, WideRank/WideRankSelect) with WideRank explicitly meant for vectors up to 2^40 bits; the docs don't give a clear size crossover for picking one over another
Building tests/benchmarks requires network access at configure time for CMake FetchContent to pull tlx and pasta-toolbox/utils
The headline select speedup depends on -march=native and x86-64 SIMD intrinsics being enabled; behavior without that flag isn't the benchmarked configuration
pick_this_over_siblings_when: None of the catalogued siblings (CRoaring, plf::bitset, better_bitset, BitLib, sul::dynamic_bitset) implement rank/select at all — they speed up direct std::bitset/std::vector<bool> operations like shifts, iteration, and set algebra. Pick pasta::bit_vector when the workload specifically needs succinct rank/select queries; for plain bit-twiddling workloads without that need, a sibling that benchmarks directly against std is the safer, lower-friction choice.
verified_claims_summary: In the SPIRE 2022 paper (arXiv:2206.01149), pasta-flat/pasta-poppy rank is up to 8% faster and pasta-flatSIMD select up to 16.5% faster than cs-poppy (Zhou, Andersen & Kaminsky, SEA'13) at matching ~3.51% space overhead, measured single-core on an AMD Ryzen 9 3950X with GCC 10.2, -O3 -march=native -DNDEBUG. Not compared directly against any C++ stdlib facility, since none offers rank/select.
status_note: Maintenance is stale (single-author, last commit 2025-04-07, 36 stars), but it's header-only and small enough to read fully and vendor; GPL-3.0 licensing is the main adoption friction, not code quality.
